_note: Admin changelog entries. Written by Claude from each commit's message, file list and size (git supplies the date, author and size). Add new entries at the top; the server inserts any new commit hash on boot and never overwrites an existing row. See docs/changelog.md.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Video Tools: animated captions look in Caption studio (word by word, Brand Kit colours and font)
entries.goal: Give Caption studio a modern look where the words follow the speech (the spoken word lights up, or words pop in one at a time), building on the server-side page renderer added for Animated title.
entries.whatChanged: Caption studio has a new Look choice: Standard subtitles (unchanged) or Animated, word by word. Animated takes the same video (upload or library) and the same SRT / script / auto-transcribe inputs. Options: how the words move (light up the spoken word, or pop in), position, size, text / spoken-word / box colours, an optional box behind the words, and a font; Brand Kit colours and heading or body font can be used (read on the server, plain 409 if missing). Each caption's time is shared out over its words by length (SRT has no word times). Words are grouped into short pages (at most 5 words, about 34 letters, stopping after punctuation). The caption strip is drawn once per word change in headless Chromium as see-through PNGs, and ffmpeg lays the picture list over the video with the soundtrack copied; a 60 s talk is about 150 pictures, not 1,800 frames. Runs as a background job (one per person, gate, Cancel, Resume). New route POST /api/videos/animated-captions. probeVideo now also returns rotation so a rotated phone video gets the right strip size (an added field only). Tutor catalogue, help box and docs updated. No new package.
filesImpacted: server/services/animatedCaptions.js (new: word timing, pages, timeline, band page, ffmpeg overlay)
server/services/animatedCaptions.test.js (new: includes a real video and Cancel)
client/src/pages/VideosPage.jsx (Look choice, animated branch of the studio, help text)
entries.benefit: Captions that follow the speech in the person's own brand, made on the server with no new package (a normal fast deploy), for short videos and social posts.
entries.concerns: Not run inside the Railway container: Chromium and ffmpeg memory and time there are unmeasured for this tool (the earlier Animated title also awaits that check), and Railway memory has had multi-GB spikes. Word timing is an estimate (time shared over the words by length), so a word can light up early or late. Tried locally on an 8 s video from a library source with Brand Kit colours and a font; not tried: a long video (limit about 1,500 words), a phone-rotated video, a video upload from the page, Cancel from the button (tested at service level). Brand text colour is the kit's onPrimary colour, which could be dark on a dark video for an unusual kit. Latin text only. The studio's Save-to-library tick does not apply to the animated look (the result has its own Save button). probeVideo's new rotation field is used only here.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Video Tools: Animated title (HTML page rendered to MP4 in a server browser, Brand Kit colours, logo and font)
entries.goal: Give Video Tools a way to make moving title screens (the ffmpeg tools only draw static or fading text), using the idea behind HyperFrames (write a page, render it to video) with the Brand Kit colours, logo and font.
entries.whatChanged: New tool Animated title in the Make group. The person types a headline and an optional supporting line, picks how it moves (slide in from the left, or fade in at the centre), the shape (widescreen, tall, square), 2 to 8 seconds and standard or Full HD, and may use the Brand Kit colours, logo and heading or body font. The server builds a small page from escaped text, a headless Chromium (Playwright, already in the image) moves its animations to each frame and takes a picture, and ffmpeg encodes the pictures to an MP4 (30 fps). A browser is started for each render and closed after it; every network request from the page except its own inline content is refused. Runs as a background job like Intro and ending (one per person, queue gate, Cancel, Resume). Brand Kit colours, logo and font are read on the server from the signed-in person's own kit; asking for one the kit lacks is a plain 409 before the job starts. Headline and supporting line use the shared mic field. Also added to the tutor chat catalogue (and its "not possible" list corrected: a title screen is possible, a title over an existing video is not), the help box and tooltips, the route inventory and docs/video-tools.md. No new package.
filesImpacted: server/services/htmlVideoRender.js (new: page to frames to MP4, cancel, network blocked)
server/services/animatedTitle.js (new: checking, page builder, Brand Kit loading)
server/services/animatedTitle.test.js (new: includes a real render and Cancel)
client/src/pages/VideosPage.jsx (menu entry, help, tooltip, tool section)
entries.benefit: Real animated titles in the person's own brand, made on the server in about 10 to 30 seconds, with no new package and so a normal fast deploy; a base for animated captions and lower-thirds later.
entries.concerns: Not run inside the Railway container: Chromium there has only been used by the Brand Kit reader, so check memory and render time after the first deploy. Measured on Windows 10 locally: 5 s at 720p about 8 s and 215 MB, at 1080p about 10 s and 640 MB (Chromium plus ffmpeg), after Railway's multi-GB memory spikes were being chased, so watch the graph. Two renders at once and the Cancel button were not tried on screen (Cancel is tested at service level; the job gate allows one render at a time). The brand body font and the 409 messages were tested with a stub database, not seen. Two movements only, no sound, one font, Latin text only, no transparent background (PNG frames were 6.6 times slower); standalone title screen, not laid over a video. The route inventory test still fails for 11 SERP Tracker routes from other work (not these).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Contract Review OCR pool uses OCR_WORKERS (default 2, was fixed 4)
entries.goal: Cut memory use: Contract Review always started 4 OCR workers, while Translate was already cut to 2 on 2026-11-07 after multi-GB memory spikes on Railway.
entries.whatChanged: The Contract Review OCR pool now reads the same OCR_WORKERS setting as Translate (1 to 8, default 2) instead of a fixed 4. It still starts only when a scanned contract needs it, handles English only, and shuts down after 5 idle minutes. The ready log line shows the real worker count. docs/env-vars.md says OCR_WORKERS now covers both pools.
entries.benefit: Less memory while Contract Review OCR is running (two fewer English workers), and one setting for both OCR pools.
entries.concerns: A scanned contract may OCR somewhat slower with 2 workers than with 4 (the scheduler queues the extra pages). Checked only that the module loads and the Translate pool test passes; no real scanned contract was run. Whether this explains the multi-GB spikes is not known: the Translate boot pool was the likelier cause and was fixed earlier. This commit has not been pushed.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics: brand font in Batch, Pipeline and saved recipes; Brand Kit button; fix Batch crash on open
entries.goal: Finish the brand font so every text tool can use it, make the Brand Kit window's main button useful, and fix a crash found while testing.
entries.whatChanged: The brand font (heading or body) now also works for the text watermark in Batch, the Pipeline "Add text" step and saved recipes. The font is loaded from the signed-in person's own Brand Kit once per batch, background job or run, and anything the browser sends as brandFonts is deleted and replaced. A recipe stores only the choice (kept only on text steps, and only if valid) and reads the font when it runs; a step that names a font the Brand Kit does not have refuses the whole batch, job or pipeline before the first picture with a plain 409 message, and the Pipeline screen shows such a choice as "Brand heading (none saved)". Font drop-downs added to Batch (watermark) and to the Pipeline text step. In the Brand Kit window the main footer button is now Download DESIGN.md when nothing typed by hand is waiting to be saved, and Save Brand Kit when the logo, colours or font name differ from the saved kit (a small Download link stays beside Clear then); a reading from a website is already saved by Use selected. Also fixes the Batch tool crashing the page when opened: its recipe lines read the batchOp state before the line that declared it, which was the case since the recipe-in-Batch commits of 2026-10-25. Guide chat, help text and docs/brand-from-url.md updated.
filesImpacted: server/routes/graphics/enhance.js (text step takes the loaded brand fonts; /pipeline loads them)
server/routes/graphics/optimise.js (prepareBatch loads fonts for op watermark and pipelines, runBatchItems passes the context)
server/services/graphicsRecipes.js (keeps a valid fontSource on text steps only)
server/routes/graphics/brandText.test.js (batch, pipeline, recipes, job, injection, other person)
entries.benefit: The brand font works everywhere text is drawn, including repeatable recipes and batches; the Brand Kit window's main button now does the useful thing; and the Batch tool opens again.
entries.concerns: The Batch crash fix is a one-line move, but the bug was in committed code since 2026-10-25, so the Batch tool is probably broken on the live site until this is deployed. A recipe that names a brand font refuses to run (whole batch, nothing processed) until the Brand Kit has that font again, by design. The Batch tool's recipe list still only refreshes after a page reload (already the case, not changed). The Brand Kit button logic compares the by-hand form with the saved kit, so an edit that is reverted by hand counts as no change. Seen in the local app on 2026-11-07: the footer flip, a Batch text watermark, a Pipeline text step and a saved recipe run through Batch, all in Montserrat; the background-job path and the 409 cases are covered by the server test, not by eye. Latin text only. Not run in the Railway container. This commit has not been pushed.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics: Watermark text and Batch Text can use the Brand Kit font
entries.goal: Carry the brand font into the two remaining text tools that most often put a name on a picture.
entries.whatChanged: Watermark (text mode) and Batch Text accept fontSource brand-heading or brand-body and draw the text as vector outlines from the stored font file, the same way Text Overlay and Composite already do; a new centredLabel helper sizes the label box from the font. Batch Text loads the font once for the whole batch, so a missing or foreign font refuses the whole request with 409 in plain words instead of failing picture by picture. A Font drop-down appears in both tools only when a font file is stored. An image watermark ignores the setting, and any other value is the old Arial path, byte for byte. Guide chat entries, help text, the (i) paragraph and docs/brand-from-url.md were updated to match.
entries.benefit: A watermark or a captioned batch in the owner's own brand font, with no effect on anyone who does not choose it.
entries.concerns: A watermark applied through Batch (op watermark) or a saved recipe, and the Pipeline text step, still use Arial: they call the watermark code with no signed-in user, so no font is loaded; fixing that means passing the user through those paths. Latin text only, as for Text Overlay. Seen in the local app on 2026-11-07: a text watermark in Montserrat (tiling and the 409 cases are covered by the server test, not by eye) and a two-picture Batch Text run whose first result was opened full size. Not run in the Railway container. This commit has not been pushed.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics Brand Kit: guide chat, help text and docs for the website reading
entries.goal: Keep the guide chat, help text and docs in step with the new feature.
entries.whatChanged: The Graphics guide chat now knows the Brand Kit's "Get from a website" box, the stored fonts, the DESIGN.md download and the Font choice in Text Overlay and Composite, and that Watermark, Batch Text and Pipeline text still use the standard font; one new "cannot do" line (sites that need a login or block automated visitors, gradient colours). No tour was added: Graphics has no tour definition to extend.

The whole series was tested together: all brand tests, the existing graphics tests, the guide and tool-count tests and a client build pass on this final tree; the earlier six commits were not built or tested one by one.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics: Text Overlay and Composite text layers can use the Brand Kit font
entries.goal: Make the brand font usable in graphics, not only stored.
entries.whatChanged: Text Overlay and the text layers of Composite accept fontSource brand-heading or brand-body. The text is drawn as vector outlines from the stored font file with opentype.js and put into the same SVG as before, so background pill, outline, alignment, wrapping, opacity and position are unchanged; this avoids the named-font problems found in the Windows/Linux check (librsvg ignores @font-face, an unregistered name falls back differently per system, colour fringes on thin strokes). Widths come from the same file, with pair kerning. A missing or unreadable brand font answers 409 in plain words and never quietly draws another font; anything else is the old Arial path. A Font drop-down appears only when a font file is stored, and Bold/Normal is greyed out for a brand font.
entries.benefit: Headlines and captions in the owner's own brand font, identical shapes on Windows and Linux, with no effect on anyone who does not choose it.
entries.concerns: Latin text only (no ligatures beyond pair kerning, no right-to-left; only the Latin part of a font is stored); a missing character draws as the font's missing-glyph box. Only Text Overlay and Composite text layers use it; Watermark, Batch Text and the Pipeline text step still use Arial. Seen in the local app on Text Overlay (plain, with pill and outline, wrapped); the Composite screen was seen with its new drop-down but a full Composite run was covered by the server test, not by eye. Not run in the Railway container. This is one of seven commits cut from finished work after the fact, so this commit's files were assembled by hand to be a coherent step; only the final tree (the last commit of the seven) was built and tested as a whole.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics Brand Kit: Download DESIGN.md
entries.goal: Give the saved Brand Kit a plain-text form that AI coding tools can read.
entries.whatChanged: A Download DESIGN.md button in the Brand Kit window. The file is built in the browser from the saved kit: colours by role with real contrast ratios, the dark look, typography with CSS font-family lines, corner style, a :root block of --brand-* variables and a few rules. Sections with nothing to say are left out and a hand-filled kit gives a smaller file; the logo picture, font file and internal names are never put in it.
entries.benefit: The brand read from a website can be dropped next to README.md in any project so a coding tool builds on-brand screens.
entries.concerns: Built and shown in the local app with the browser download intercepted, so the text was read but the actual file save to disk was not exercised. The sans-serif fall-back in the CSS lines is a guess and the file says so. The rules are generic. This is one of seven commits cut from finished work after the fact, so this commit's files were assembled by hand to be a coherent step; only the final tree (the last commit of the seven) was built and tested as a whole.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics Brand Kit: "Get from a website" in the Brand Kit window
entries.goal: Let the owner use the reader from the Brand Kit window.
entries.whatChanged: A "Get from a website" box at the top of the Brand Kit window: address (with microphone, Enter reads), the global processing window with steps and Cancel, then a preview of swatches by role, a corner sample, the heading and body fonts drawn in the real downloaded files, and logo candidates; the owner ticks what to keep and presses Use selected. Saving the Brand Kit by hand now carries over fields the window does not show (it replaced the whole value before and would have erased them), typing a different font name drops the stored heading file, and Clear also removes the stored font files. Pure helpers live in brandSiteLogic.mjs, named differently from the component because on Windows (and so in Vite) BrandFromSite and brandFromSite are the same file name and the wrong one was imported.

entries.benefit: Filling the Brand Kit from a website in one step, with nothing saved until the owner presses Use selected.
entries.concerns: Seen working locally on 2026-11-07 on one real site (read, preview, Use selected, hand save kept the new fields, Clear emptied them, a private address showed a plain error). Not looked at: phone width, dark theme and the other four themes, pressing Cancel mid-read. Two bugs were found by using it and fixed in this commit (the same-name import, and a flag that stayed off after React's development double mount). This is one of seven commits cut from finished work after the fact, so this commit's files were assembled by hand to be a coherent step; only the final tree (the last commit of the seven) was built and tested as a whole.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics Brand Kit: keep a website reading (graphics_brand_fonts table, Use this route)
entries.goal: Keep a chosen reading: store the font files and save the ticked parts into the Brand Kit safely.
entries.whatChanged: New table graphics_brand_fonts (the converted font file, one heading and one body row per person, role and extension checked). POST /api/graphics/brand-from-url/:id/apply copies only the ticked parts (colours, corners, logo, heading font, body font) into the Brand Kit JSON in settings and the font table in one transaction (the kit row is locked; a failure rolls both back). The font is re-checked first (TrueType/OpenType header, 4 MB cap, the recorded sha256, the BrandFont name); only a PNG logo is accepted. A name-only font replaces the kit's font name and removes an older stored file for that role. Also GET (list, file) and DELETE routes for the stored fonts. New optional kit fields (roles, palette, dark, radius, headingFont, bodyFont, source) never disturb a kit without them; fields the code does not know are kept.
entries.benefit: A reading becomes part of the Brand Kit without a half-saved state, and the kit JSON that every Graphics tool loads stays small.
entries.concerns: A new table is created on the next boot (idempotent, small). Font files are kept as bytea, up to 4 MB each and two per person. Not put in the recycle bin on purpose (a reading can be repeated), which the owner may want to reverse. Tested against a scratch Postgres schema using the real table definition, and the cross-user ownership sweep passed, but its log did not name the new routes, so the unit test is the evidence for the owner-only rule. This is one of seven commits cut from finished work after the fact, so this commit's files were assembled by hand to be a coherent step; only the final tree (the last commit of the seven) was built and tested as a whole.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics Brand Kit: POST /api/graphics/brand-from-url and a short-lived proposal store
entries.goal: Expose the reader to the Brand Kit screen without sending font files to the browser.
entries.whatChanged: POST /api/graphics/brand-from-url reads one site and returns the proposal; GET .../:id/font/:role serves the converted font for a preview. The proposal and its fonts are kept in server memory for 30 minutes (6 per person, 120 in all) under a random id that only the person who made it can use. One read at a time per person and 12 an hour. Errors are plain words; the log records the host only. Route inventory updated.
entries.benefit: The screen can show a preview with the real fonts while megabytes of font data never travel to the browser and back.
entries.concerns: The store is in memory per server instance, so a restart or a different instance during a rolling deploy loses a reading (the person reads again); the 12 an hour and one-at-a-time limits are per instance too. Tested with a stubbed reader and once end to end by hand against a live site. This is one of seven commits cut from finished work after the fact, so this commit's files were assembled by hand to be a coherent step; only the final tree (the last commit of the seven) was built and tested as a whole.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics Brand Kit: read a website's colours, fonts, corners and logo (server reader)
entries.goal: Let Graphics learn a brand (colours, fonts, corners, logo) from any public website, as the first step of filling the Brand Kit from a URL.
entries.whatChanged: New server reader: opens one public page in the Chromium the Browser Agent already uses (desktop, phone and dark-mode looks) and proposes colour roles, heading and body fonts as plain TTF/OTF files, a corner style and logo candidates. Colours are weighted by how much of the page they cover, with cookie bars and sale banners damped. Font files seen on the page are converted from woff2 with fontTools (already installed), cut to one weight if variable, and renamed to a unique plain name so sharp draws exactly the file's outlines; Google Fonts is the fall-back. Every request the page makes, including every redirect leg, is checked with checkSsrf through the browser's request-pause protocol. Nothing is exposed or saved yet.
entries.benefit: A real reading of a site's look instead of a guess, with no new dependency and no Dockerfile or package.json change, so no slow deploy.
entries.concerns: Colours come from computed styles, so gradients and background images are not counted (on stripe.com the main colour came out green, not purple). A font whose CSS name differs from the name inside its file (stripe.com's sohne-var) is not matched, so only its name is kept. Chromium resolves names itself after the address check, so DNS rebinding is not fully covered (acceptable for a signed-in tool). A read takes 10 to 30 seconds and a few hundred MB of browser, at most 2 at once. Tried by hand on two real sites only. Not reachable from the app yet.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Admin Changelog page, with the first 25 entries and a rule to add one per commit
entries.goal: Give the owner one place to see what each update did, what it touched, why, what it gained and what to watch, and make sure it is kept up to date.
entries.whatChanged: New admin-only Changelog page (Business menu, /changelog). Entries are grouped by Day, Week (Monday start), Month or Year and each opens to show what changed, the code impacted, the goal, the benefit and the concerns; a "Concerns" tag shows on rows that have one, and Expand all opens everything. Entries are loaded on boot by commit hash from a JSON file and never overwrite an existing row. The first 25 entries (4 to 7 Nov 2026) were written from the git history. CLAUDE.md and docs/changelog.md now require an entry for every commit, added in a "Changelog:" commit before pushing.
entries.benefit: A readable history of the app's changes for the owner, with risks called out, and a standing rule that keeps it current.
entries.concerns: The entry text is Claude's reading of each commit's message and file list, so it says what a commit claims to do and is not proof it works. The changelog is only as current as the rule is followed: nothing writes entries automatically or blocks a push without one. The route-manifest test still fails on 11 SERP Tracker routes that were already missing before this commit (not caused by it).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Shares: 9-step guided tour of the whole page
entries.goal: Give the Shares page the guided tour that every tool is meant to have.
entries.whatChanged: A 9-step tour of the whole Shares page: quotes and the tab row, Trades and Cash as the source, CGT/Statements/Accountant pack, Charts and News, Questions, Thesis, Metals and where to get help. It switches tabs as it goes and returns to Portfolio. It starts from a "Take the tour" link beside the title or from Settings, Tours (/shares?tour=1), and starting it closes the first-visit info box that would otherwise sit behind it.
entries.benefit: New and returning users get a walk through every Shares tab, including the new Thesis tab, and the tour can be retaken from Settings.
entries.concerns: Checked in a browser on a local copy (all 9 steps, no console errors, finishing sets the done flag). The wording makes claims about each tab, so it needs updating when a tab changes; a tab added later gets no step until someone adds one and updates the step count in the file.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Shares: Thesis tab with AI thesis check
entries.goal: Let the owner write down why each share is owned and what would prove them wrong, then test that against what Vault already stores.
entries.whatChanged: New Thesis tab in Shares: per-holding thesis, assumptions, red lines and value anchors, with a "Check now" that rates each assumption and scores the thesis. The score and verdict are worked out in code, not by the AI, and any downgrade has to quote evidence. Deleting goes to the recycle bin. Guide chat, info box, docs and roadmap updated.
entries.benefit: A written record of why a share is held and a dated history of whether the reasons still stand, without the app ever saying buy, sell or hold.
entries.concerns: The live AI call had not been run when this shipped, only a stubbed one, so the first real check needs reading critically. The evidence is only Vault's own trades and news briefings (no company filings), so many ratings will say "not enough evidence". The Shares page container is narrow, so the two-column layout is cramped on a wide screen.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Video Tools: AI look for planners, shot changes, thumbnail suggestions, caption provenance
entries.goal: Make the slideshow and join planners smarter, and make clip trimming and thumbnails easier.
entries.whatChanged: Opt-in "Let the AI look" on the Slideshow and Join planners (off every time, small JPEG copies made in the browser, cost shown first, server cap VIDEO_VISION_MAX_USD default $0.25). Clip timeline gets Find shot changes, Previous/Next shot and snap markers. Thumbnail gets "Suggest good frames" (browser only, free). YouTube example prefers written captions over automatic ones and shows who wrote them.
filesImpacted: client/src/pages/videos/ (planners, ClipTimeline, ThumbnailSuggest, sceneScan and helpers)
entries.benefit: Better ordering suggestions for photos and clips, faster trimming at real shot changes, and clearer caption quality, with spend limited by a visible cap.
entries.concerns: When the AI look is switched on, frames from the person's own footage go to the AI provider. It costs money each time (capped, but a cap is still spend). The commit is large (24 files, about 1,400 lines added) and the message does not say how shot detection was checked on real footage.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Memory: tooltips, (i) box, tour, microphone and a guide chat, like Finance and Video Tools
entries.goal: Bring the Memory page up to the same help standard as Finance and Video Tools.
entries.whatChanged: Tooltips on every control and no browser pop-ups (delete asks "Delete? Yes / No" on the row), an (i) "How Memory works" box, a 6-step tour, a microphone on both text boxes, and a Memory guide chat on the shared guide code with tests that fail if the page and the guide drift apart. Wording corrected: memories are added only on the Memory page, and deleting is permanent.
entries.benefit: Memory is easier to learn and use, and the help text now matches what the app really does.
entries.concerns: Adds one more AI-backed route (the guide). Deleting a memory is permanent with no recycle bin and no undo, which the commit documents but does not change.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Route guard: let administrators in, like the menu and the server
entries.goal: Stop administrators being bounced to the home page from a feature that is switched off.
entries.whatChanged: The page route guard now lets admins in when a feature flag is off, matching the menu and the server, which already did. Members are still sent home.
entries.benefit: An admin can open Memory (off by default) from the menu without being redirected.
entries.concerns: Behaviour change: admins can now open any feature-off page. That matches the server, but a feature that is meant to look "off" for everyone will still be reachable by admins.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: re-read misses, daily tracking (standard queue, off by default), new keywords
entries.goal: Make rank checks more trustworthy and add daily tracking.
entries.whatChanged: A lookup that misses for a site is read again (up to 3 reads), and "not found" is only reported when every read missed. Daily tracking per site, off by default, with a cost estimate shown first: standard queue, top 30, misses re-read in up to 3 rounds, monthly cap checked before every round, failures saved as failed. New serp_rankings table and a Tracked rankings section. Keywords gets a "New this period" filter.
entries.benefit: Fewer false "not ranked" answers, and rankings tracked over time without manual lookups.
entries.concerns: Spends money on DataForSEO (a real depth-30 search cost US$0.0018). It is off by default with an estimate and a monthly cap, but re-reads multiply the cost. A large change (27 files, 1,160 lines).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Memory page: show the real error instead of "undefined memories stored"
entries.goal: Stop the Memory page saying "undefined memories stored" when something fails.
entries.whatChanged: load() used to store an error reply as if it were the list or the summary. A failing stats call now shows a red banner with the server's reason and the rest of the page keeps working; a failing list shows its error instead of crashing.
entries.benefit: A real, readable error instead of a confusing broken page.
entries.concerns: This shows the error but does not fix whatever made /api/memory/stats fail in the first place; the cause needs finding separately.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Memory: translate OCR pool on demand, memory log; SERP Tracker: Keywords tab (Search Console history)
entries.goal: Cut a high, spiky Railway memory bill, and add Search Console keyword history to the SERP Tracker.
entries.whatChanged: Translate's OCR pool is now built on first use, shut down after 5 idle minutes and defaults to 2 workers (it used to build 4 workers x 8 languages at every boot, about 575 MB of ~860 MB resting memory locally). New server/lib/memoryLog.js writes a line every 5 minutes with Node and container memory, and extra detail on a 300 MB jump. SERP Tracker gets a Keywords tab backed by Search Console history (16-month backfill, daily update at 7:00 am Brisbane, just-off-page-1 filter, per-keyword chart, slipped-keyword alerts).
entries.benefit: Lower and steadier hosting memory, a log that explains future spikes, and an early warning when keywords slip.
entries.concerns: The first translation after an idle period is slower while the OCR pool starts, and 2 workers may slow several OCR jobs at once. The memory saving was measured locally; the commit does not confirm the Railway bill has dropped. Two unrelated changes share one commit (23 files, 1,659 lines), which makes it harder to revert one without the other.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: "Use my location" and "Use Australia" for the search place
entries.goal: Make it easy to set the place a search is run from.
entries.whatChanged: "Use my location" reads the browser position, names the suburb through the shared geocoder and matches it to DataForSEO's place list; "Use Australia" resets it. It only fills the box and nothing saves until Save. An empty box still means Australia.
entries.benefit: Local-search results can match where the business actually is, without hunting for a place code.
entries.concerns: Needs the browser's location permission and the geocoder to answer; if the suburb does not match a DataForSEO place the person has to choose another.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: Google site setting (google.com.au) and a "Searching as" place label
entries.goal: Search the Australian Google index and show the real place used.
entries.whatChanged: Site setup gets a Google site setting (default google.com.au) sent as se_domain, plus a free check against DataForSEO's Australian place list that shows the place actually used (for example Bowen Hills, place 9060847). Docs record the LLM Search Cloud project for the Google OAuth client.
entries.benefit: Ranks should be closer to what a person on google.com.au sees, and the app is honest about the place it searched.
entries.concerns: This re-adds, as a setting, the se_domain idea that was reverted earlier the same day (d43297e8). The commit does not state that it fixed the gap between the tracker's page 2 and the real page 1, so that still needs checking against a real search.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Revert "SERP Tracker: send se_domain so Australia searches the google.com.au index"
entries.goal: Undo the automatic se_domain change from c27c23de.
entries.whatChanged: Reverts c27c23de, which always sent se_domain so Australia searched the google.com.au index.
entries.benefit: Returns the code to its previous known behaviour.
entries.concerns: The commit message does not say why it was reverted. The idea came back a few hours later as a visible setting (b43ef801).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: send se_domain so Australia searches the google.com.au index
entries.goal: Fix ranks that differed from what a person on google.com.au sees.
entries.whatChanged: DataForSEO echoed se_domain google.com for location Australia, so a site on page 2 here was page 1 (#2) for a real user. The request now always sends se_domain so Australia searches the google.com.au index.
entries.benefit: Aimed to make tracked positions match real Australian results.
entries.concerns: Reverted by d43297e8 about 1.5 hours later, so it did not stay in. Always sending the domain for every site was probably too blunt, which the later setting (b43ef801) addresses.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: several sites (one per client), CRM client link, Find my site, honest coverage
entries.goal: Let one person track several sites (one per client) and find where a site ranks deep in the results.
entries.whatChanged: Up to 20 sites per person (each domain once) with a site switcher and Add/Delete with Undo (recycle bin type serp-site), an optional CRM client link, and a Quick lookup with no site. Find my site searches up to depth 200 with the expected cost shown first. Short pages from DataForSEO are recorded as coverage and retried (max 4) within the cost cap. A real queued-mode answer is kept as a parser fixture.
entries.benefit: Works for an agency with many clients, and tells the truth about how deep a search really read.
entries.concerns: Deep searches with retries are the most expensive thing in the tool (shown first and capped). One of the biggest commits in the set (27 files, about 1,970 lines added, 480 removed), so it carries more regression risk.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: keep the real Live answer as a parser fixture, with a test that reads it
entries.goal: Keep a real DataForSEO Live answer as a test fixture.
entries.whatChanged: Adds the real Live answer for "walk in wine cabinets" (Australia, desktop, top 10, AI summary on). serpParse.test.js now parses it against values read off it by hand. It holds only the search request and Google's public results, no credentials or account details.
entries.benefit: The parser is tested against a real answer rather than an invented one.
entries.concerns: None noted. A fixture is a snapshot, so it will not catch later changes in the real answer format.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker Lookup: read real websites from Google redirect links, show ads and "searched as"
entries.goal: Stop the parser missing the owner's own site.
entries.whatChanged: A real Live answer showed most organic results as google.com/goto redirect links with domain google.com and the real site only in the breadcrumb, so the site could never be found. The parser now reads the site from the breadcrumb, says "not found but some results hide their website" rather than a flat not-ranked, lists sponsored ads (or says none came back) and shows what DataForSEO says it searched (Google site, place, language).
entries.benefit: Real rankings are found, and the result explains uncertainty instead of reporting a false miss.
entries.concerns: Depends on the shape of Google's results as relayed by DataForSEO, which can change. Older saved lookups say ads were not recorded.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: Lookup tab, saved lookups with select and delete, guide chat and info box
entries.goal: Add a Lookup tab so a single live search can be run and kept.
entries.whatChanged: Lookup runs a live DataForSEO search and parses position, boxes above, AI Overview citations, the top 10 and page layout. It logs the cost before parsing, honours the monthly cap and saves the result (latest 50, raw answer kept 90 days). Saved lookups can be opened, ticked and deleted through the shared recycle bin with Undo. Adds the SERP Tracker guide chat, (i) box and tooltips.
entries.benefit: A quick, costed way to see exactly how a keyword looks on Google today, with a history to look back on.
entries.concerns: Each lookup is a paid call. Raw answers are stored for 90 days, which adds database size.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker stage 2: queued search calls and the depth cost test script
entries.goal: Add the cheaper queued search method and a script to measure its cost.
entries.whatChanged: postSerpTask, getSerpTask and waitForSerpTask for DataForSEO's Standard Queue with unit tests, DataForSEO's own message on 4xx errors, and server/scripts/serpDepthTest.js, a one-search cost test that never re-posts.
entries.benefit: A route to much lower per-search cost, and a safe way to find out what depth really costs.
entries.concerns: Not yet run against a real search when committed: DataForSEO answered 403 until the account was verified. Later commits show it working (depth 30 cost US$0.0018).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker stage 1: site profile, daily run, DataForSEO balance check, cost log
entries.goal: Start the SERP Tracker tool: site profile, a daily run and cost logging.
entries.whatChanged: New preview tool (flag serpTracker, off by default) at /serp-tracker. Saves the tracked site's settings, runs a daily job at 20:00 UTC (6 am Brisbane) that checks the DataForSEO balance and logs every call's cost, and records each run as ok or failed. The run engine takes independent modules so later stages plug in unchanged.
entries.benefit: Foundation for tracking search rankings with spend visible from day one.
entries.concerns: Introduces a scheduled job that calls a paid API; it runs under the cron single-flight lock and the tool is off by default. Stage 1 only checks the balance and logs costs, so it does not track rankings yet.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Usage page: info box, guide chat and tooltips
entries.goal: Give the Usage page the standard help set.
entries.whatChanged: Adds an info box, a Usage guide chat (route, service, registry entry and tests) and tooltips.
entries.benefit: The page explains itself and answers questions about where spend comes from.
entries.concerns: None noted. The commit has no message body beyond its title.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Usage page: modern layout and Advice tab on model choice
entries.goal: Modernise the Usage page and help choose cheaper models.
entries.whatChanged: New layout and an Advice tab on model choice, backed by a new usageInsights service and changes to the cost calculator and usage route.
entries.benefit: Spend is easier to read, and there is concrete guidance on which model to use for what.
entries.concerns: The advice is only as good as the usage data it reads, so its first suggestions are worth sanity-checking before acting. A large rewrite of the page (670 lines added, 262 removed) with no commit message explanation.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Web Extractor palette: group colours, show where each is used
entries.goal: Make the colour palette easier to read.
entries.whatChanged: Colours are grouped and the page shows where each one is used.
entries.benefit: The palette tells the designer where a colour matters, not only that it exists.
entries.concerns: None noted. The commit has no message body beyond its title.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Web Extractor palette: join near-identical shades, skip platform defaults, show main colours first
entries.goal: Cut noise from the palette result.
entries.whatChanged: Near-identical shades are joined, platform default colours are skipped and the main colours are shown first.
entries.benefit: A shorter, more useful list that reflects the brand rather than the framework.
entries.concerns: Joining near-identical shades uses a closeness threshold, so two colours meant to be different could be merged. The commit has no message body.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Web Extractor: add Colour palette tool
entries.goal: Add a tool that finds the colours a website uses.
entries.whatChanged: New Colour palette tool in the Page group. It counts colours from linked and imported style files, <style> blocks, style="" attributes and the theme-color meta, normalises them to #rrggbb, counts roles (background, text, border, other) and follows CSS variables and aliases. It suggests a primary, accent, background and text colour and splits brand colours from greys, whites and blacks. Optional "Pages to read" (1, 3 or 6). Swatches copy the hex, with Copy hex codes, Copy as CSS and Download CSV.
entries.benefit: Pulls a site's real colour scheme into a usable palette in seconds.
entries.concerns: Reading several pages means more requests to someone else's site, though they go through the app's existing safe-fetch checks and each page is fetched once. The "one page only" wording elsewhere now has this exception.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Domain page: pick up names in single quotes, add spotted names automatically
entries.goal: Recognise names the person puts in single quotes and add them automatically.
entries.whatChanged: Anything in double, curly or single quotes counts as a name (a single quote only when it opens a word, so apostrophes are safe). Names spotted in the description are added to "Names I already have" when Generate is pressed, unless removed with the x on their chip. The brief shows a tip about the quotes rule.
entries.benefit: Less retyping, and names the person already chose are built into the suggestions.
entries.concerns: A quoted phrase that is not a name could be added. It can be removed with the chip's x. This reverses the previous commit's "never added automatically".

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Domain page: use the names you mention, and talk the names through
entries.goal: Build domain suggestions around names the person already has and let them talk the names through.
entries.whatChanged: Names spotted in the description (a book called X, an artist named Y, quoted titles, runs of capitalised words) are offered as one-click "Names I already have". Names are built around those: ownCombos joins the title or person with the brief's words, and candidates built on an own name rank first and are not penalised. "Talk it through" adds a question box (POST /api/domains/ask, answered from the names and their checks, changes nothing) and a notes box that triggers a new round. The last 12 turns are saved with the set.
entries.benefit: Suggestions reflect the person's own names, and they can ask why or refine the brief without starting over.
entries.concerns: A new AI route (ask) that costs per question. The ranking change favours own-name candidates, so check the results are not crowded by them. A large commit (26 files).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Domain generation: stop long rounds timing out
entries.goal: Stop long domain-generation rounds timing out.
entries.whatChanged: The wide list is now written by two AI calls at once (about 90 names each, 150 s each) instead of one call for 180 names; one failing is fine, both timing out gives a clear 504 telling the person to try again or pick a faster model. Every DomScan request times out after 20 s. A time budget per round: no new domain lookup starts after 170 s and explanations are skipped past 200 s, so a slow AI step cannot push the request past the hosting gateway limit.
entries.benefit: Generation finishes or fails clearly instead of hanging until the gateway cuts it off.
entries.concerns: On a slow round the time budget means fewer availability checks and no explanations, so a round can return a thinner list. Two parallel AI calls double the call count for each round.
